html:
Peter von Scholten was governor general of the Danish West Indies who declared all enslaved people free on 3 July 1848, as thousands of them marched on the fort at Frederiksted on St Croix.

Denmark had decided on a gradual end to slavery over twelve years. The enslaved would not wait. Led by a man known as General Buddhoe, they gathered and threatened to burn the town. Von Scholten, who had already eased conditions, proclaimed freedom on his own authority.

He was recalled to Denmark and tried for overstepping his powers, then cleared. Emancipation Day, 3 July, is a holiday in the islands. Freed workers stayed bound by harsh labour laws, which led to the Fireburn thirty years later, in a Danish colony then in decline.
sum: Peter von Scholten was governor general of the Danish West Indies who declared all enslaved people free on 3 July 1848, as thousands of them marched on the fort at Frederiksted on St Croix.
